title: 6 simple tweaks I use to get two days of battery from my Galaxy Watch 9
summary: Battery life continues to be a struggle for Galaxy Watch owners.
body: When the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 was first announced, one of the features that excited me most was the larger battery. I actually upgraded to a 44mm model, so I was expecting a significant improvement in battery life compared to my 40mm Watch 8. However, in practice, I found that it lasted roughly the same amount of time. Even so, I don’t have to charge it daily, and that’s thanks to a handful of tweaks that get me two days instead. These tweaks balance usability with battery saving so that you don’t give up too many features in the quest to extend battery life.

title: ‘True Family’: Nile Rodgers Remembers Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor
summary: "RIP my dear friend. We were always happy when we were together. I love you," Rodgers writes.
body: You can’t choose you family. But you can choose your true family . That’s how Nile Rodgers remembers Andy Taylor , the founding guitarist of Duran Duran and The Power Station, who died this week following a years-long battle with prostate cancer, at the age of 65 . Rodgers, like millions of music fans around the globe, is mourning the Englishman’s passing. “Dear Andy Taylor RIP. How many countless great days and nights did we have?,” he writes. “I was sleeping last night when I heard the news of your passing. #RIP my dear friend. We were always happy when we were together. I love you.” Rodgers and Taylor go way back. The Chic mainstay and elite record producer worked with Duran Duran on many of their hits, a friendship that began with the British new wave legends’ first U.S. No. 1 “The Reflex” from 1984. Chic’s bass player Bernard Edwards produced the 1985 debut album from The Power Station, which gathered Duran Duran’s Andy and John Taylor, along with English singer Robert Palmer and U.S. drummer Tony Thompson. Rodgers provided some informal assistance to the project, which yielded the hits “Some Like It Hot” and a cover of Marc Bolan’s “Get It On (Bang A Gong)”. “ #Bernard…

body: TL;DR Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 is rolling out in South Korea with groundwork for hands-free message management. Similar capabilities were spotted in China in September, but global versions of Samsung Messages still lack these additions. Samsung may have shut down its Messages app in the US in July , but that hasn’t stopped the company from developing new features for users elsewhere. The latest update rolling out in South Korea suggests Samsung is preparing its texting app for a future where AI assistants can do much more than help you write messages. title: Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting
summary: Android just recorded its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, with Apple's iOS bucking the trend.
body: TL;DR Android accounted for 74% of global smartphone sales in Q3 2026, down five points from a year ago and its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, per Counterpoint Research. iOS climbed to a record Q3 share of 21% as iPhone sales grew year-on-year, even as the overall market shrank 16%. HarmonyOS held at 5% globally and took 22% of China’s market, with HUAWEI growing 12% while China’s market shrank 10%. The memory shortage has been dragging down phone sales all year, and new data shows it may be hurting Android more than its rivals. According to Counterpoint Research , global smartphone sales fell 16% year-on-year in Q3 2026, a sharper drop than the 11% decline seen in Q2. Android’s share of those sales slipped to 74%, down from 79% in Q3 2025. That’s the lowest share Android has ever posted in a third quarter, though it’s still a touch above the 72% it hit in Q4 2025, when new iPhones typically give Apple a seasonal bump.

title: Google is working on gamepad profiles for Android’s controller remapping feature
summary: You might not have to remap your controller every time you launch a different game.
body: TL;DR Google is working on adding support for multiple gamepad profiles in Android. Code in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 hints at a new interface for managing gamepad profiles. The feature could let users switch between gamepad button layouts on the fly. If you’re a mobile gamer, you probably use controllers for many Android games . Customizing a controller’s layout can be quite useful, especially if you like using different layouts for different games. Although Google added support for game controller remapping with Android 17 , it currently lets you keep only one layout saved at a time. Fortunately, Google is now working to improve the feature with support for multiple gamepad profiles. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. While digging through the code in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 , we spotted several strings that point to an upcoming gamepad profile management interface. According to the strings, there could be a “Default” profile, along with options to edit and delete individual profiles. We also spotted strings hinting at a “More options” menu for each profile.

title: These are the best times to buy a new phone if you want to save money
summary: Don’t pay full price for your next flagship. Here’s when Samsung, Google and Apple phones get their biggest discounts.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority Buying a flagship phone on launch day without a good trade-in deal is one of the easiest ways to overspend in 2026. Smartphone prices are shooting northwards, largely because of growing demand for AI components in data centers and constrained supply for practically everything else, including smartphones. You’d be surprised to learn that memory costs have gone from accounting for 13% of a phone’s total component costs in early 2025 to more than 40% by late 2026. As a result, major brands have passed those costs on to buyers. Flagships like the Apple iPhone 18 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro now start $100 higher than their predecessors and spending well over $1,000 on a new phone is becoming the norm.

title: The Blurams F20C solar camera sees what my video doorbell misses
summary: This outdoor security camera was able to solve my problem.
body: Credit: Andy Baryer / Android Authority My doorbell camera works great at showing who’s at my front door. However, it leaves me with a couple of blind spots. First, it doesn’t show my package at the bottom of the door when it’s delivered. If I’m not home, that package might sit there for hours, making it vulnerable to theft by a porch pirate. My low-tech solution was to put a sign under the door asking the driver to place the package into a box next to my door. However, this creates a second blind spot because my doorbell camera doesn’t show packages going into the box. With the Blurams F20C 4K Solar Outdoor Security Camera, my goal was to eliminate these two blind spots. I mounted it to a tree that faces my front door so I can see if the driver leaves the package at the front door or if they put it into the delivery box. So, is a solar-powered camera with no wires reliable enough to keep watch over my deliveries all day?

title: Samsung is killing Quick Share’s Private sharing, and it’s already gone in One UI 9.5 beta
summary: A Galaxy Store update warns of the upcoming shutdown, while One UI 9.5 Beta 1 removes the toggle and code entirely.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has added an advance notice to the Galaxy Store changelog for Quick Share version 13.9.10.5 warning that it plans to discontinue the Private sharing feature. Once the shutdown takes effect, users will not be able to send or receive files through Private sharing, and recipients will lose access to previously shared files. Samsung has not announced a specific cutoff date, though the toggle and code are already removed in Quick Share v13.9.50.30 on One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Samsung’s Quick Share has evolved rapidly this year, gaining features like AirDrop compatibility on the Galaxy S26 series and preparing for Tap to Share in One UI 9.5 . However, not every tool is making the cut. Samsung is now officially warning users that it plans to discontinue Quick Share’s Private sharing feature. The warning appears in the Galaxy Store changelog for Quick Share version 13.9.10.5, which lists an “Advance notice of the upcoming discontinuation of the ‘Private sharing’ feature”.

title: Android 17 is getting a new setting to prevent unwanted Bluetooth audio switching
summary: Google looks set to borrow a handy feature from Apple's iOS 26 playbook.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google is working on a new Android 17 feature that lets users keep audio playing through their headphones even when another device connects. The feature, called Keep audio in headphones, should appear in Connection preferences once it goes live. It’s similar to Apple’s Keep Audio with Headphones feature from iOS 26, which prevents audio from switching to a car or other connected device. Google could soon make one small but useful change to how Android handles Bluetooth audio . We’ve spotted a new feature in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 that could let users keep audio playing through their headphones even when another audio device, such as a car stereo or Bluetooth speaker, connects to their phone. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. We spotted the feature, called “Keep audio in headphones,” in the latest Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 build. The setting comes with a straightforward description: “Always play audio in your headphones when other audio devices like speakers and cars connect to this device.”

title: Pixel’s upcoming Priority notifications could cut the line and get colorful highlights
summary: Google could also rebadge Notification Intelligence as Notification organizer.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing a new AI-powered Priority notification that will show up at the top of your notifications shade. These time-sensitive notifications could also get colorful highlights to make them pop. This is part of a larger reshuffle where Notification Intelligence could be renamed Notification organizer. Last December, Google introduced Notification organizer to help rein in notification overload by muting unwanted notifications and grouping low-priority ones into a summary. On Pixel phones, this is part of Notifications Intelligence, and Google now appears to be working to include a new feature to emphasize high-priority notifications. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. We’ve discovered that Google is now working to add a new feature called Priority notifications under Notification organizer. Like Samsung’s One UI and iOS, this feature will display notifications that it deems time-sensitive or important at the top of the notifications shade. Based on the description, these notifications could also have a special color treatment to make them stand out more.

title: Motorola’s Android 17 update breaks cover screen calling features for some Razr users
summary: Making a call without unfolding your Razr just got harder.
body: TL;DR Some Motorola Razr users report losing access to the dial pad and contacts on the cover screen after updating to Android 17. The issue appears to stem from Motorola replacing its native Phone app with Google’s, with no easy way to switch back. Rotating the phone or reducing the display and font sizes has helped some affected users restore the missing functionality. One of the biggest selling points of Motorola’s Razr phones is how much you can do without ever unfolding them. We’ve previously put this versatility to the test , but something as basic as making a phone call from the cover screen is now proving difficult for some Razr owners following the Android 17 update. Affected users say the update replaced Motorola’s native Phone app with Google’s alternative. While the new app works as expected on the main display, the cover screen experience is different. Users report that they can still access recent calls but can no longer open the dial pad or access contacts without opening the phone.
